Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
Spring has arrived and with the highly anticipated 
promise of milder weather comes also some annual 
events that attract huge interest here in Fingal including 
Seachtain na Gaeilge and of course the fantastic St. 
Patrick’s Day celebrations both guaranteed to provide 
fun and entertainment for people of all ages. 
 
Seachtain na Gaeilge will be celebrated from March 1st – 
17th and there are a number of Council events taking 
place in County Hall Swords, in partnership with the 
Seamus Ennis Arts Centre, in Local Libraries and 
Ardgillan Demesne as well as many other events being 
organised by Irish language groups throughout the 
County. Irish is a language that thrives through use and 
isn’t just for those well versed in the language – it is for 
everyone to use and whether you are recalling the Irish 
of your schooldays or learning for the first time, this is 
the perfect time to become immersed in the culture 
through speaking the language. The popularity of our 
Gaeltacht Scholarship Scheme is testament to the 
enthusiasm and grá for the Irish language as young 
people across Fingal prepare to spend time in Gaeltacht 
areas to improve their knowledge. This year, there were 
500 applications to the scheme which provides financial 
assistance for 15 successful applicants who are 
attending Irish college in the summer months. To 
mention just a couple of events taking place over this 
fortnight - Seachtain na Gaeilge’s annual celebration 
with Ceol, Craic and Gaeilge will take place in the Atrium, 
County Hall on Wednesday, March 11th from 7 to 9pm 
and is brought to you with support from The Séamus 
Ennis Arts Centre. Talented musicians Éamonn de Barra, 
Paudie O’Connor, and Aoife Ní Chaoimh will be 
performing on the night and everyone is welcome to 
come along and experience this celebration of music 
and culture. Always a popular event, the Pop-Up 
Gaeltacht comes to the Séamus Ennis Arts Centre on 
March 19th starting at 5.30pm followed by their regular 
bilingual singing session. To discover all the fantastic 
events which will be held over Seachtain na Gaeilge, you 
can go to https://www.fingal.ie/seachtain-na-gaeilge-
2026 for full details.  
 
Staying with the theme of pride in our language and 
culture, St. Patrick’s Day will be celebrated with eight 
parades across Fingal showcasing the best in music, 
dance and family friendly fun!  
 
 
 
Our annual celebration of our patron saint has attracted 
many thousands of excited spectators over the years 
and this year will be no exception as local groups, sports 
clubs and performers don their colours and wave their 
flags proudly on the day. Parades will take place in 
Swords, Blanchardstown, Balbriggan, Malahide, Rush, 
Lusk, Skerries and Donabate and all the start times, 
routes and details are available here:  
https://www.fingal.ie/events/st-patricks-day-parades a 
new Best Dressed Group prize for entrants to the 
Blanchardstown, Balbriggan, Swords and Malahide 
parades is sure to encourage groups to think creatively 
this year as there is a chance of winning €1,000 for first 
place, €500 for second and third place. In the run up to 
the big day, our local libraries, community spaces and

Management Team this month as she retires from

colleagues across a variety of roles in Louth, Dún 
Laoghaire-Rathdown and Fingal County Councils. Her 
expertise and experience were particularly put to the 
test as she steered the Operations & Water Services 
teams through the Covid era and has overseen many

I wish to congratulate Mary T on her many  
accomplishments and thank her for her many years of 
diligent public service. I know you will join me in wishing 
Mary T. a long, happy and healthy retirement.    
 
 
Best wishes,

Digital Statistics

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
 
Destination Brand Launch 
 
The new destination tourism brand, Explore Fingal, 
was officially launched on Monday 23rd February 
2026 at a gala event in the Grand Hotel, Malahide. 
 
Page 5 
Local media personality Simon Delaney was MC. The 
launch unveiled a new brand identity, dedicated 
website, and social media platforms, marking a 
significant milestone in the implementation of the 
Fingal Tourism Strategy 2024–2029. 
The event was officially launched by the Mayor of 
Fingal Cllr Tom O’Leary, and he informed the 200 
attendees representing all areas of tourism in the 
Fingal area that “The launch of Explore Fingal, the 
new destination tourism brand, is a significant step 
in consolidating and highlighting the tourism offering 
within Fingal.”  
 
 
 
 
The launch of the new destination brand was a great 
opportunity 
to 
demonstrate 
the 
Council’s 
commitment to delivering on its tourism and 
economic development ambitions, underpinned by 
sustainability and the parallel implementation of the 
Fingal Food & Drink Policy 2024–2029.  
The new destination website, www.ExploreFingal.ie 
is now live.

Progression of the Advisory Group and Four 
Strategic Groups 
Following the inaugural Strategic Group meetings in 
2025, the first quarterly meetings of 2026 were 
successfully convened in January, marking continued 
delivery of the Fingal Tourism, Food & Drink 
Framework. The four Strategic Groups are now fully 
operational and meeting on an agreed annual cycle. 
The Advisory Group convened for its second meeting 
on 23rd February 2026, where members were 
presented with progress updates on the Framework 
and received reports from each Strategic Group 
Chair outlining key action areas and priorities. 
It continues to provide strategic oversight, facilitate 
collaboration, monitor progress, and offer expert 
guidance, with a clear focus on delivering achievable 
actions within the lifetime of the Framework while 
maintaining a longer-term strategic lens to inform 
future opportunities and investment decisions.

ECCD 
with

Architects 
Department are undertaking a thorough assessment

Skerries Mills. The sail arms were badly damaged 
during Storm Bram. This work is being done with a 
view to engaging a specialist contractor shortly. It is 
our intention that the much-loved landmark of the 
Skerries landscape is substantively restored to its 
former glory during 2026.

Malahide Castle 
On the 18th March the Visitor Centre at Malahide will 
host a showcase for the Fingal Food Circle as part of 
a pre-conference reception for 200 EU CAP 
practitioners. The attendees will be from 27 countries 
and are all agricultural advisors who are attending a 
two-day briefing in the Grand Hotel. 
  
ECCD has worked with Fingal LEADER and other Irish 
partners to ensure that local attractions, amenities 
and restaurants are promoted. This is to encourage 
the idea that the delegates can return to the area to 
enjoy an exceptional tourism offering, especially 
excellent sustainable food offering and local 
experiences.  
 
 
 
Malahide Castle has also won the Public Sector 
Magazine award for National Tourism Impact in 
2025. The award is peer-based, and was secured this 
year due to the excellent ongoing conservation work 
being undertaken in the Castle, and the integration 
of this into the guided tour experience.  
 
 
 
Page 8 
 
In a similar vein Malahide Castle has won the 2025 
award for excellence by CIE Tours. CIE used guest 
feedback from a survey of over 30,000 visitors to 
hundreds of sites in Ireland. Malahide emerged with 
a satisfaction rating of 92%, and this result is best in 
class for visitor attractions. It is a testament to the 
quality of the experience in the Castle and Gardens 
tours.

Arts Act Grant Scheme 2026 
 
This year marked the first time that the Arts Act Grant 
Scheme was publicly announced as open for 
applications. In tandem with this, a new Revenue 
Strand was introduced by invitation only in this pilot 
year, expanding the scope of the scheme and the 
range of applicants eligible to apply. 
As a result of these changes, the scheme attracted 
60% new applicants in this funding round. Overall, 
this represented a 140% increase in applicants 
compared to 2025. This public announcement 
indicated a significantly increased awareness of the 
scheme and broadened extent of support sought to 
€730,714. 
A total of 84 applications were received and 
assessed. Having examined the applications, the 
panel has recommended 38 awards, amounting to a 
total sum of €225,000. 
Events, festivals and projects supported under this 
scheme aim to deliver quality arts experiences to 
participants and audiences, to increase opportunities 
for participation and engagement in the arts and to 
contribute to the development of the arts in the 
county.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit, 
which is also referred to as a notice of termination, 
from their landlord may be worried or unsure of 
what to do.  Fingal County Council and the Dublin 
Regional Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to 
advise anyone affected of the services that are 
available to them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff 
in the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide 
a Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in 
the Dublin Region, including Fingal. Threshold can 
also be contacted directly on Freephone 1800 454 
454 or via their website www.threshold.ie which 
contains more information and advice on the validity 
of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice 
on applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising 
the person on the level of Housing Assistance 
Payment (HAP) they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.   
 
Page 71 
Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal with 
tenancy issues that may require an inter-authority 
approach.  In particular, we are working closely with 
our colleagues in the other Dublin Local Authorities 
on the implementation of the Government policy and 
guidance, with a focus on the needs of tenants.   
  
Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with 
potential acquisitions of properties with tenants in 
situ, any acquisition is subject to appropriate due 
diligence and checks before any commitment is 
made to acquire, including, for example, determining 
that a valid notice of termination is in place, the 
tenant has a social housing need, and the condition 
and valuation of the property.  
  
The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to 
remain in their homes, including schemes to support 
the purchase of homes and a Cost Rental in-situ 
Scheme. The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ Scheme is 
available for tenants who are not eligible for social 
housing and are at risk of homelessness. The DHLGH 
has advised that local authorities are to be the first 
point of contact for this scheme, but it is managed by 
the Housing Agency. Under the scheme, the Housing 
Agency can purchase a property and rent it to the 
tenant. Fingal County Council will undertake an initial 
assessment of the tenant’s circumstances and refer 
details to the Housing Agency for consideration, 
where the tenant is at risk of homelessness and the 
Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ scheme applies. The 
Housing Agency will then contact the landlord about 
the purchase of the property.  
  
Where a tenant wishes to purchase their home from 
the landlord, local authorities can provide advice 
about the Local Authority Home Loan scheme. The 
Government is examining implementing a ‘right of 
first refusal’ for tenants to purchase their homes, as 
well as expanding the First Home shared equity 
scheme. The Council will be able to provide more 
information on these when available.

By-Product Notifications 
Soil and Stones from excavations at construction 
sites are one of the major waste streams generated 
by construction, and are often managed as a By-
Product, as opposed to waste material, whereby they 
can be re-used at other sites, as long as a number of 
criteria are fulfilled: 
• 
the material was produced as an integral part 
of the production process 
• 
further use of the material is certain 
• 
further use is lawful - planning permission, 
no adverse impacts 
• 
no additional processing is required. 
By-product notifications are registered with the EPA 
and Local Authorities are alerted. The Waste 
Enforcement & Regulation Section then has a role to 
play in reviewing these notifications, through 
desktop assessments and on-site inspections to 
ensure the By-Product criteria are complied with and 
no environmental pollution is generated. A total of 21 
notifications of by-product soil and stone were made 
in February - 13 were desktop verified and 5 site 
inspections were carried out.
